headline: Ivanti zero-day and an exploited Windows Shell bypass lead a heavy patch week
standfirst: Two actively exploited flaws — one in an edge remote-access appliance, one buried in Microsoft's record Patch Tuesday — dominate the day, alongside a critical Ghostscript RCE, a local-root Linux kernel bug, a phishing-infrastructure disruption and UK sanctions on a crypto payment conduit.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA is telling administrators to patch an Ivanti Connect Secure flaw immediately, describing it as exploited in zero-day attacks since at least the beginning of October [[s14]]. The supplied structured record for this story carries no CVE identifier and no KEV enrichment, so the specific vulnerability ID, severity and catalog status are not confirmed here; the urgency rests on the reported in-the-wild exploitation and the agency's guidance. Analysis: an authentication bypass in a remote-access appliance is the kind of foothold that tends to attract follow-on intrusion, but the supplied evidence gives no attribution, affected versions or post-exploitation detail, so those stay unknown.

Microsoft's Patch Tuesday shipped fixes for a record 1,413 vulnerabilities [[s29]], but the one to triage first is CVE-2026-96951: a Windows Shell security-feature bypass that is confirmed exploited and present in CISA's KEV catalog, listed there as a Windows command-injection issue (CWE-77). NVD scores it 8.8 High under CVSS 3.1, vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R — network-reachable with no privileges required, but user interaction required, so it should not be described as zero-click. CISA's required action directs US federal agencies to apply mitigations under BOD 26-04, with a due date only a few days after the KEV addition; that is a federal requirement, not a universal deadline.

## Industry

Microsoft says its Digital Crimes Unit facilitated a disruption of a Chinese-language cybercrime ecosystem that coupled phishing-kit operators tracked as Storm-2990 with a marketplace tracked as Storm-3119 selling tools and infrastructure, working alongside law enforcement agencies and other partners worldwide [[s13]]. The operation is tied to more than a billion malicious messages. The supplied excerpt names none of the specific agencies, courts or countries involved, so those details cannot be stated.

The United Kingdom has sanctioned Cryptomus, a cryptocurrency platform that experts describe as a major conduit for payments tied to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services, and as helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions [[s3]].

## Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-74580, dubbed Vghost, is a Linux vhost bug scored 8.8 High under CVSS 3.1 on a local vector (AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N) with changed scope [[s26]]. Per the supplied description, the vring metadata cache that vhost treats as proof a region was already validated is not reset when VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR replaces the descriptor, available and used rings, nor when VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM changes region sizes; with a device IOTLB attached, the stale cache keeps translating through a mapping that no longer covers the address. The reported result: local kernel memory read and write and root across nearly a decade of kernel versions, and in one virtualization configuration a guest writing into host memory and hijacking the program that runs the virtual machine. Tencent Zhuque Lab is credited with the find. The KEV check is a confirmed miss for this CVE, which does not establish that exploitation has not occurred.

CVE-2026-39919 in Ghostscript is the day's highest-scoring item: a heap-based buffer overflow rated 9.3 Critical under CVSS 4.0 (CWE-122) in the JPEG 2000 output adapter, affecting Ghostscript before 10.08.0 [[s41]]. A crafted PDF with mismatched component subsampling factors drives the non-samescale sub-byte-depth output path to allocate a row buffer sized for packed output while writing a full byte per column, corrupting chunk-allocator metadata to reach code execution. The supplied vector records network reachability, no privileges and no user interaction; delivery still depends on a crafted document reaching a Ghostscript-based pipeline, a condition the vector does not capture. Here too the KEV check is a confirmed miss, not proof that exploitation has not occurred.

## Research

Talos and Recorded Future attribute UAT-6275, described as Kazakhstan-nexus, to intrusions against government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States, with recovered artifacts showing additional apparent interest in water resources and energy [[s6]]. The excerpt supplies no tooling, timeline or victim detail, and the attribution is the researchers' assessment.

ThreatFabric has detailed Hirudo, an Android banking trojan that replaces legitimate banking apps with purpose-built patched versions designed to defeat the apps' own in-app security checks, with replacements identified for eight Indonesian banking apps [[s22]]. Analysis: the defensive check now runs inside the attacker's build, so it cannot be relied on; the excerpt does not describe distribution channels or victim counts.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost: reset the vring metadata cache on vring reconfiguration

vq->meta_iotlb[] caches the vhost_iotlb_map that backs each vring
metadata region, and iotlb_access_ok() returns early on a cache hit,
taking the hit as proof that the region has already been validated:

	if (vhost_vq_meta_fetch(vq, addr, len, type))
		return true;

The cache is reset on VHOST_IOTLB_UPDATE and VHOST_IOTLB_INVALIDATE, on
device IOTLB (re)initialisation and on vq reset, but not when
VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR replaces vq->desc, vq->avail and vq->used, nor when
VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM changes the region sizes.

With a device IOTLB attached both ioctls are accepted while the vq is
live, and neither validates the addresses at ioctl time: vq_access_ok()
and vq_log_used_access_ok() return true early because the addresses are
GIOVAs, deferring validation to prefetch time.  Once the cache has been
populated that deferred validation no longer runs -- vq_meta_prefetch()
hits the stale entry and returns true -- and vhost_vq_meta_fetch() keeps
translating through the old mapping as

	map->addr + addr - map->start

for an address the mapping no longer covers.  vhost_copy_to_user() and
vhost_copy_from_user() consume the result with __copy_to_user() and
__copy_from_user(), which do not check it either, so a subsequent used
ring update or descriptor fetch accesses memory outside the region the
IOTLB actually maps.

Reset the metadata cache whenever the vring is reconfigured, so the new
addresses are pushed back through iotlb_access_ok()'s slow path.

selected.title: Ghostscript flaw lets hackers hijack servers via PDF uploads
selected.excerpt: A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-39919) in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine could allow remote code execution through specially crafted PDF files. [...]

nvd.description: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the JPEG 2000 output adapter (base/sjpx_openjpeg.c) that allows attackers to cause memory corruption by supplying a crafted PDF containing a JPEG 2000 image with mismatched component subsampling factors. When image components declare different subsampling values, the non-samescale sub-byte-depth output path allocates a row buffer sized for packed output but writes a full byte per output column regardless of bit depth, overflowing the allocation and corrupting internal chunk-allocator metadata to achieve code execution.

selected.angle: A critical (CVSS 9.3) Ghostscript heap overflow (CVE-2026-39919) turns crafted PDFs into remote code execution, a serious risk for any pipeline that renders untrusted documents.
